canonical_predicate_remap.why: Same treatment as underground-maintenance-grant.json: the authored normative predicate HOLDS_CAPABILITY (actor -> capability held) is NOT in the canonical seed vocabulary, and interning it would violate the ZERO-new-symbols invariant. The relations below already carry the canonical predicate; this block records the authored intent as prose.

HOLDS_CAPABILITY.note: actor HOLDS_CAPABILITY capability becomes actor USED capability, source stays the actor, so a bounded reader still materializes the held set from OUTGOING USED edges — exactly what universe_query::read_actor_capability_set walks.

content.objective: Grant authority:construct-revision to ONE revision authority, as an attributable graph edge a bounded reader can materialize. Revising a canonical construct — its objective, its invariants, the protocol every other construct conforms to — is a heavier act than changing a file, and it must be held by an actor, not by whoever happens to run a binary. The grant is DATA only; whether a revision is admitted is decided by the protocol's revision_gate against the read set, never by this fixture.
content.deliberately_not_granted: No session body — no sponsored visitor, no arriving MCP session — receives this capability. A visitor may perceive the protocol and propose a revision; it may not enact one. That asymmetry is the point of the gate, and it is why the grant names exactly one actor.

content.description: Usage note over the existing canonical USED predicate for a construct-revision grant. Mints no symbol. A bounded read of an actor's outgoing USED edges to capability targets materializes exactly what that actor holds. Holding authority:underground-maintenance does not confer authority:construct-revision: the sets are read verbatim and the ports are separate. Authority over the ground is not authority over the law.

content.note: The exact capability string the construct protocol's revision gate (port:l2:mind-universe:construct-validity:revision-gate-v0) requires to revise a construct in place. Distinct from authority:underground-maintenance: changing a file under the city and revising the protocol the city's constructs conform to are different powers, and neither implies the other.
content.scope: Revising a construct that APPLIES_IN construct-validity-v0: its member content, its authored relations, and the retirement of relations it no longer authors. It does not confer injection of a new construct, deletion of an entity, or any external effect.

content.name: Construct revision authority
content.note: Holds authority:construct-revision via a canonical USED edge (authored HOLDS_CAPABILITY). The held set is what a bounded read returns; this note is not itself the authority. An actor that is not this one — including every embodied session body — fails closed at the revision gate.
content.accountability: Every revision admitted through this actor commits an EffectReceipt Moment naming it, in the SAME transaction as the change, so no revision of a canonical construct exists without an attributable holder behind it.

content.statement: The construct revision authority was granted authority:construct-revision by this approved authority fixture. The grant is attributable to this changeset. No other actor was granted it, and the plain citizen and every session body remain without it — which is what makes a refusal at the revision gate a real decision rather than an empty-set artifact.

content.justification: The revision authority holds authority:construct-revision (canonical USED edge; authored HOLDS_CAPABILITY); this is the sole edge that admits a construct revision at the protocol's revision gate.
